newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi's Buyoya ready for Zaire peace role.
newsitem.headline: Burundi's Buyoya ready for Zaire peace role.

text.p: Burundi's military leader Pierre Buyoya, isolated by regional states who have imposed sanctions, said he is ready to play a role in a regional conference on the conflict in eastern Zaire.

Speaking at a news conference late on Thursday, Buyoya also denied allegations by Zairean authorities that Burundi was arming ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels who control the Rusizi plain on Burundi's Zaire frontier.

"The government welcomes all the initiatives that could help to bring about a durable peace in the Great Lakes region. We are waiting for more details on the objectives of a (peace) conference and what Burundi can do to help," Buyoya said.

"Burundi once again absolutely rejects the allegation by Zairean authorities that we are involved in this conflict and invites Zaire to produce evidence of our involvement," said Buyoya, installed as leader after the July coup by the Tutsi-dominated army.

The U.N. has called for a regional summit to discuss the roots of conflict in the Great Lakes area, but Zaire has declared itself unwilling to attend and it remains unclear if Burundi would be represented.
Burundi is under regional sanctions because of the coup by the military, which is fighting Hutu rebels.
Hundreds of thousands of Burundian and Rwandan refugees have fled camps in Zaire's Kivu region because of fighting between Zaire and Banyamulenge rebels opposed to Zaire's government.
Analysts say the eastern Zaire conflict offers Buyoya a golden opportunity to end his exclusion by regional states if he can present himself as a neutral who favours peace.
Regional leaders, keen to avert a wider war, could be forced to include Buyoya in their discussions as Burundi's de facto leader.
Regional states including Tanzania, Kenya and Zaire imposed economic and transport sanctions against Buyoya, six days after he took power in a military coup on July 25.
